name: mail2deck
description: Forward an email → get a finished, on-brand presentation. Self-hosted, local LLM, grounding + critique guard, human-in-the-loop. No cloud.

paragraphs: Forward an email → get a finished, on-brand presentation. Runs on your own hardware, against any OpenAI-compatible LLM, with a grounding/critique guard and a human-in-the-loop gate.

The deck above — cover, summary, content slides, figures pulled from a linked paper, and closing — was generated end to end from the request email on the left. No template file, no manual design, no cloud AI service (the native path renders in well under a minute; web-fetch adds an opt-in network call for the figures).

Most "AI PPT" tools are cloud SaaS: your content leaves your infrastructure and the model invents freely. mail2deck is built for the opposite — run it locally, keep a tight leash on grounding, and make the human the final gate. Every outbound network call is opt-in, and no LLM ever runs in the render path.
features: Any OpenAI-compatible LLM — vLLM, Ollama, llama.cpp, or a hosted API. Reasoning-model aware (auto-disables chain-of-thought for clean JSON).

Native branded output, no template needed — the native backend draws a fully branded 16:9 deck (cover, summary, section dividers, footers, page numbers, closing) from a small Theme (colours + font + wordmark). Ships…

Grounding + critique guard — an adversarial LLM pass checks every claim against the source (sourceref per slide), flags hallucinations, missing info, tone, and classification markers (configurable). A marker hit stops…
Two render backends — native (deterministic python-pptx, approved text verbatim) or presenton (AI-designed themed decks; richer, looser grounding).
Web enrichment (opt-in) — fetch URLs found in the prompt (browser-grade TLS impersonation for bot-protected pages) and pull page text + images into the deck.
